bsb.5:14: Yet more and more believers were brought to the Lord—large numbers of both men and women.
bsb.5:15: As a result, people brought the sick into the streets and laid them on cots and mats, so that at least Peter’s shadow might fall on some of them as he passed by.
bsb.5:16: Crowds also gathered from the towns around Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those tormented by unclean spirits, and all of them were healed.
bsb.5:17: Then the high priest and all his associates, who belonged to the party of the Sadducees, were filled with jealousy. They went out
bsb.5:18: and arrested the apostles and put them in the public jail.
bsb.5:19: But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the jail and brought them out, saying,
bsb.5:20: “Go, stand in the temple courts and tell the people the full message of this new life.”
bsb.5:21: At daybreak the apostles entered the temple courts as they had been told and began to teach the people. When the high priest and his associates arrived, they convened the Sanhedrin—the full assembly of the elders of Israel—and sent to the jail for the apostles.
bsb.5:22: But on arriving at the jail, the officers did not find them there. So they returned with the report:
bsb.5:23: “We found the jail securely locked, with the guards posted at the doors; but when we opened them, we found no one inside.”
bsb.5:24: When the captain of the temple guard and the chief priests heard this account, they were perplexed as to what was happening.
bsb.5:25: Then someone came in and announced, “Look, the men you put in jail are standing in the temple courts teaching the people!”
bsb.5:26: At that point, the captain went with the officers and brought the apostles—but not by force, for fear the people would stone them.
bsb.5:27: They brought them in and made them stand before the Sanhedrin, where the high priest interrogated them.
bsb.5:28: “We gave you strict orders not to teach in this name,” he said. “Yet you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching and are determined to make us responsible for this man’s blood.”
bsb.5:29: But Peter and the other apostles replied, “We must obey God rather than men.
bsb.5:30: The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you had killed by hanging Him on a tree.
bsb.5:31: God exalted Him to His right hand as Prince and Savior, in order to grant repentance and forgiveness of sins to Israel.
bsb.5:32: We are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey Him.”
bsb.5:33: When the Council members heard this, they were enraged, and they resolved to put the apostles to death.
bsb.5:34: But a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law who was honored by all the people, stood up in the Sanhedrin and ordered that the men be put outside for a short time.
bsb.5:35: “Men of Israel,” he said, “consider carefully what you are about to do to these men.
bsb.5:36: Some time ago Theudas rose up, claiming to be somebody, and about four hundred men joined him. He was killed, all his followers were dispersed, and it all came to nothing.
bsb.5:37: After him, Judas the Galilean appeared in the days of the census and drew away people after him. He too perished, and all his followers were scattered.
bsb.5:38: So in the present case I advise you: Leave these men alone. Let them go! For if their purpose or endeavor is of human origin, it will fail.
bsb.5:39: But if it is from God, you will not be able to stop them. You may even find yourselves fighting against God.”
bsb.5:40: At this, they yielded to Gamaliel. They called the apostles in and had them flogged. Then they ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and released them.
bsb.5:41: The apostles left the Sanhedrin, rejoicing that they had been counted worthy of suffering disgrace for the Name.
bsb.5:42: Every day, in the temple courts and from house to house, they did not stop teaching and proclaiming the good news that Jesus is the Christ.
bsb.6:1: In those days when the disciples were increasing in number, the Grecian Jews among them began to grumble against the Hebraic Jews because their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution of food.
bsb.6:2: So the Twelve summoned all the disciples and said, “It is unacceptable for us to neglect the word of God in order to wait on tables.
bsb.6:3: Therefore, brothers, select from among you seven men confirmed to be full of the Spirit and wisdom. We will appoint this responsibility to them
bsb.6:4: and will devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word.”
bsb.6:5: This proposal pleased the whole group. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, as well as Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas from Antioch, a convert to Judaism.
bsb.6:6: They presented these seven to the apostles, who prayed and laid their hands on them.
bsb.6:7: So the word of God continued to spread. The number of disciples in Jerusalem grew rapidly, and a great number of priests became obedient to the faith.
bsb.6:8: Now Stephen, who was full of grace and power, was performing great wonders and signs among the people.
bsb.6:9: But resistance arose from what was called the Synagogue of the Freedmen, including Cyrenians, Alexandrians, and men from the provinces of Cilicia and Asia. They began to argue with Stephen,
bsb.6:10: but they could not stand up to his wisdom or the Spirit by whom he spoke.
bsb.6:11: Then they prompted some men to say, “We heard Stephen speak words of blasphemy against Moses and against God.”
bsb.6:12: So they stirred up the people, elders, and scribes and confronted Stephen. They seized him and brought him before the Sanhedrin,
bsb.6:13: where they presented false witnesses who said, “This man never stops speaking against this holy place and against the law.
bsb.6:14: For we have heard him say that Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs that Moses handed down to us.”
bsb.6:15: All who were sitting in the Sanhedrin looked intently at Stephen, and they saw that his face was like the face of an angel.
bsb.7:1: Then the high priest asked Stephen, “Are these charges true?”
bsb.7:2: And Stephen declared: “Brothers and fathers, listen to me! The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran,
bsb.7:3: and told him, ‘Leave your country and your kindred and go to the land I will show you.’
bsb.7:4: So Abraham left the land of the Chaldeans and settled in Haran. After his father died, God brought him out of that place and into this land where you are now living.
bsb.7:5: He gave him no inheritance here, not even a foot of ground. But God promised to give possession of the land to Abraham and his descendants, even though he did not yet have a child.
bsb.7:6: God told him that his descendants would be foreigners in a strange land, and that they would be enslaved and mistreated four hundred years.
bsb.7:7: ‘But I will punish the nation that enslaves them,’ God said, ‘and afterward they will come forth and worship Me in this place.’
bsb.7:8: Then God gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision, and Abraham became the father of Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day. And Isaac became the father of Jacob, and Jacob of the twelve patriarchs.
bsb.7:9: Because the patriarchs were jealous of Joseph, they sold him as a slave into Egypt. But God was with him
bsb.7:10: and rescued him from all his troubles. He granted Joseph favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh king of Egypt, who appointed him ruler over Egypt and all his household.
bsb.7:11: Then famine and great suffering swept across Egypt and Canaan, and our fathers could not find food.
bsb.7:12: When Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent our fathers on their first visit.
bsb.7:13: On their second visit, Joseph revealed his identity to his brothers, and his family became known to Pharaoh.
bsb.7:14: Then Joseph sent for his father Jacob and all his relatives, seventy-five in all.
bsb.7:15: So Jacob went down to Egypt, where he and our fathers died.
bsb.7:16: Their bones were carried back to Shechem and placed in the tomb that Abraham had bought from the sons of Hamor at Shechem for a price he paid in silver.
bsb.7:17: As the time drew near for God to fulfill His promise to Abraham, our people in Egypt increased greatly in number.
bsb.7:18: Then another king, who knew nothing of Joseph, arose over Egypt.
bsb.7:19: He exploited our people and oppressed our fathers, forcing them to abandon their infants so they would die.
bsb.7:20: At that time Moses was born, and he was beautiful in the sight of God. For three months he was nurtured in his father’s house.
bsb.7:21: When he was set outside, Pharaoh’s daughter took him and brought him up as her own son.
bsb.7:22: So Moses was educated in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and was powerful in speech and action.
bsb.7:23: When Moses was forty years old, he decided to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.
bsb.7:24: And when he saw one of them being mistreated, Moses went to his defense and avenged him by striking down the Egyptian who was oppressing him.
bsb.7:25: He assumed his brothers would understand that God was using him to deliver them, but they did not.
bsb.7:26: The next day he came upon two Israelites who were fighting, and he tried to reconcile them, saying, ‘Men, you are brothers. Why are you mistreating each other?’
bsb.7:27: But the man who was abusing his neighbor pushed Moses aside and said, ‘Who made you ruler and judge over us?
bsb.7:28: Do you want to kill me as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?’
bsb.7:29: At this remark, Moses fled to the land of Midian, where he lived as a foreigner and had two sons.
bsb.7:30: After forty years had passed, an angel appeared to Moses in the flames of a burning bush in the desert near Mount Sinai.
bsb.7:31: When Moses saw it, he marveled at the sight. As he approached to look more closely, the voice of the Lord came to him:
bsb.7:32: ‘I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.’ Moses trembled with fear and did not dare to look.
bsb.7:33: Then the Lord said to him, ‘Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.
bsb.7:34: I have indeed seen the oppression of My people in Egypt. I have heard their groaning and have come down to deliver them. Now come, I will send you back to Egypt.’
bsb.7:35: This Moses, whom they had rejected with the words, ‘Who made you ruler and judge?’ is the one whom God sent to be their ruler and redeemer through the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
bsb.7:36: He led them out and performed wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, at the Red Sea, and for forty years in the wilderness.
bsb.7:37: This is the same Moses who told the Israelites, ‘God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers.’
bsb.7:38: He was in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our fathers. And he received living words to pass on to us.
bsb.7:39: But our fathers refused to obey him. Instead, they rejected him and in their hearts turned back to Egypt.
bsb.7:40: They said to Aaron, ‘Make us gods who will go before us! As for this Moses who led us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.’
bsb.7:41: At that time they made a calf and offered a sacrifice to the idol, rejoicing in the works of their hands.
bsb.7:42: But God turned away from them and gave them over to the worship of the host of heaven, as it is written in the book of the prophets: ‘Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?
bsb.7:43: You have taken along the tabernacle of Molech and the star of your god Rephan, the idols you made to worship. Therefore I will send you into exile beyond Babylon.’
bsb.7:44: Our fathers had the tabernacle of the Testimony with them in the wilderness. It was constructed exactly as God had directed Moses, according to the pattern he had seen.
bsb.7:45: And our fathers who received it brought it in with Joshua when they dispossessed the nations God drove out before them. It remained until the time of David,
bsb.7:46: who found favor in the sight of God and asked to provide a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.
bsb.7:47: But it was Solomon who built the house for Him.
bsb.7:48: However, the Most High does not dwell in houses made by human hands. As the prophet says:
bsb.7:49: ‘Heaven is My throne and the earth is My footstool. What kind of house will you build for Me, says the Lord, or where will My place of repose be?
bsb.7:50: Has not My hand made all these things?’
bsb.7:51: You stiff-necked people with uncircumcised hearts and ears! You always resist the Holy Spirit, just as your fathers did.
bsb.7:52: Which of the prophets did your fathers fail to persecute? They even killed those who foretold the coming of the Righteous One. And now you are His betrayers and murderers—
bsb.7:53: you who received the law ordained by angels, yet have not kept it.”
bsb.7:54: On hearing this, the members of the Sanhedrin were enraged, and they gnashed their teeth at him.
bsb.7:55: But Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, looked intently into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.
bsb.7:56: “Look,” he said, “I see heaven open and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.”
bsb.7:57: At this they covered their ears, cried out in a loud voice, and rushed together at him.
bsb.7:58: They dragged him out of the city and began to stone him. Meanwhile the witnesses laid their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
bsb.7:59: While they were stoning him, Stephen appealed, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.”
bsb.7:60: Falling on his knees, he cried out in a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” And when he had said this, he fell asleep.
bsb.8:1: And Saul was there, giving approval to Stephen’s death. On that day a great persecution broke out against the church in Jerusalem, and all except the apostles were scattered throughout Judea and Samaria.
bsb.8:2: God-fearing men buried Stephen and mourned deeply over him.
bsb.8:3: But Saul began to destroy the church. Going from house to house, he dragged off men and women and put them in prison.
bsb.8:4: Those who had been scattered preached the word wherever they went.
bsb.8:5: Philip went down to a city in Samaria and proclaimed the Christ to them.
bsb.8:6: The crowds gave their undivided attention to Philip’s message and to the signs they saw him perform.
bsb.8:7: With loud shrieks, unclean spirits came out of many who were possessed, and many of the paralyzed and lame were healed.
bsb.8:8: So there was great joy in that city.
bsb.8:9: Prior to that time, a man named Simon had practiced sorcery in the city and astounded the people of Samaria. He claimed to be someone great,
bsb.8:10: and all the people, from the least to the greatest, heeded his words and said, “This man is the divine power called the Great Power.”
bsb.8:11: They paid close attention to him because he had astounded them for a long time with his sorcery.
bsb.8:12: But when they believed Philip as he preached the gospel of the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.
bsb.8:13: Even Simon himself believed and was baptized. He followed Philip closely and was astounded by the great signs and miracles he observed.
bsb.8:14: When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them.
bsb.8:15: On their arrival, they prayed for them to receive the Holy Spirit.
bsb.8:16: For the Holy Spirit had not yet fallen upon any of them; they had simply been baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
bsb.8:17: Then Peter and John laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
bsb.8:18: When Simon saw that the Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles’ hands, he offered them money.
bsb.8:19: “Give me this power as well,” he said, “so that everyone on whom I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit.”
bsb.8:20: But Peter replied, “May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could buy the gift of God with money!
bsb.8:21: You have no part or share in our ministry, because your heart is not right before God.
bsb.8:22: Repent, therefore, of your wickedness, and pray to the Lord. Perhaps He will forgive you for the intent of your heart.
bsb.8:23: For I see that you are poisoned by bitterness and captive to iniquity.”
bsb.8:24: Then Simon answered, “Pray to the Lord for me, so that nothing you have said may happen to me.”
bsb.8:25: And after Peter and John had testified and spoken the word of the Lord, they returned to Jerusalem, preaching the gospel in many of the Samaritan villages.
bsb.8:26: Now an angel of the Lord said to Philip, “Get up and go south to the desert road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza.”
bsb.8:27: So he started out, and on his way he met an Ethiopian eunuch, a court official in charge of the entire treasury of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians. He had gone to Jerusalem to worship,
bsb.8:28: and on his return was sitting in his chariot reading Isaiah the prophet.
bsb.8:29: The Spirit said to Philip, “Go over to that chariot and stay by it.”
bsb.8:30: So Philip ran up and heard the man reading Isaiah the prophet. “Do you understand what you are reading?” Philip asked.
bsb.8:31: “How can I,” he said, “unless someone guides me?” And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.
bsb.8:32: The eunuch was reading this passage of Scripture: “He was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and as a lamb before the shearer is silent, so He did not open His mouth.
bsb.8:33: In His humiliation He was deprived of justice. Who can recount His descendants? For His life was removed from the earth.”
bsb.8:34: “Tell me,” said the eunuch, “who is the prophet talking about, himself or someone else?”
bsb.8:35: Then Philip began with this very Scripture and told him the good news about Jesus.
bsb.8:36: As they traveled along the road and came to some water, the eunuch said, “Look, here is water! What is there to prevent me from being baptized?”
bsb.8:38: And he gave orders to stop the chariot. Then both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
bsb.8:39: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord carried Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no more, but went on his way rejoicing.
bsb.8:40: But Philip appeared at Azotus and traveled through that region, preaching the gospel in all the towns until he came to Caesarea.
bsb.9:1: Meanwhile, Saul was still breathing out murderous threats against the disciples of the Lord. He approached the high priest
bsb.9:2: and requested letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so that if he found any men or women belonging to the Way, he could bring them as prisoners to Jerusalem.
bsb.9:3: As Saul drew near to Damascus on his journey, suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.
bsb.9:4: He fell to the ground and heard a voice say to him, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?”
bsb.9:5: “Who are You, Lord?” Saul asked. “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,” He replied.
bsb.9:6: “Now get up and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do.”
bsb.9:7: The men traveling with Saul stood there speechless. They heard the voice but did not see anyone.
bsb.9:8: Saul got up from the ground, but when he opened his eyes he could not see a thing. So they led him by the hand into Damascus.
bsb.9:9: For three days he was without sight, and he did not eat or drink anything.
bsb.9:10: In Damascus there was a disciple named Ananias. The Lord spoke to him in a vision, “Ananias!” “Here I am, Lord,” he answered.
bsb.9:11: “Get up!” the Lord told him. “Go to the house of Judas on Straight Street and ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul, for he is praying.
bsb.9:12: In a vision he has seen a man named Ananias come and place his hands on him to restore his sight.”
bsb.9:13: But Ananias answered, “Lord, many people have told me about this man and all the harm he has done to Your saints in Jerusalem.
bsb.9:14: And now he is here with authority from the chief priests to arrest all who call on Your name.”
bsb.9:15: “Go!” said the Lord. “This man is My chosen instrument to carry My name before the Gentiles and their kings, and before the people of Israel.
bsb.9:16: I will show him how much he must suffer for My name.”
bsb.9:17: So Ananias went to the house, and when he arrived, he placed his hands on Saul. “Brother Saul,” he said, “the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road as you were coming here, has sent me so that you may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”
bsb.9:18: At that instant, something like scales fell from Saul’s eyes, and his sight was restored. He got up and was baptized,
bsb.9:19: and after taking some food, he regained his strength. And he spent several days with the disciples in Damascus.
bsb.9:20: Saul promptly began to proclaim Jesus in the synagogues, declaring, “He is the Son of God.”
bsb.9:21: All who heard him were astounded and asked, “Isn’t this the man who wreaked havoc in Jerusalem on those who call on this name? And hasn’t he come here to take them as prisoners to the chief priests?”
bsb.9:22: But Saul was empowered all the more, and he confounded the Jews living in Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Christ.
bsb.9:23: After many days had passed, the Jews conspired to kill him,
bsb.9:24: but Saul learned of their plot. Day and night they watched the city gates in order to kill him.
bsb.9:25: One night, however, his disciples took him and lowered him in a basket through a window in the wall.
bsb.9:26: When Saul arrived in Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.
bsb.9:27: Then Barnabas brought him to the apostles and described how Saul had seen the Lord, who spoke to him on the road to Damascus, and how Saul had spoken boldly in that city in the name of Jesus.
bsb.9:28: So Saul stayed with them, moving about freely in Jerusalem and speaking boldly in the name of the Lord.
bsb.9:29: He talked and debated with the Grecian Jews, but they tried to kill him.
bsb.9:30: When the brothers learned of this, they took him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.
bsb.9:31: Then the church throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria experienced a time of peace. It grew in strength and numbers, living in the fear of the Lord and the encouragement of the Holy Spirit.
bsb.9:32: As Peter traveled throughout the area, he went to visit the saints in Lydda.
bsb.9:33: There he found a man named Aeneas, who had been paralyzed and bedridden for eight years.
bsb.9:34: “Aeneas,” Peter said to him, “Jesus Christ heals you! Get up and put away your mat.” Immediately Aeneas got up,
bsb.9:35: and all who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord.
bsb.9:36: In Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha (which is translated as Dorcas), who was always occupied with works of kindness and charity.
bsb.9:37: At that time, however, she became sick and died, and her body was washed and placed in an upper room.
bsb.9:38: Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples heard that Peter was there and sent two men to urge him, “Come to us without delay.”
bsb.9:39: So Peter got up and went with them. On his arrival, they took him to the upper room. All the widows stood around him, weeping and showing him the tunics and other clothing that Dorcas had made while she was still with them.
bsb.9:40: Then Peter sent them all out of the room. He knelt down and prayed, and turning toward her body, he said, “Tabitha, get up!” She opened her eyes, and seeing Peter, she sat up.
bsb.9:41: Peter took her by the hand and helped her up. Then he called the saints and widows and presented her to them alive.
bsb.9:42: This became known all over Joppa, and many people believed in the Lord.
bsb.9:43: And Peter stayed for several days in Joppa with a tanner named Simon.
bsb.10:1: At Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, a centurion in what was called the Italian Regiment.
bsb.10:2: He and all his household were devout and God-fearing. He gave generously to the people and prayed to God regularly.
bsb.10:3: One day at about the ninth hour, he had a clear vision of an angel of God who came to him and said, “Cornelius!”
bsb.10:4: Cornelius stared at him in fear and asked, “What is it, Lord?” The angel answered, “Your prayers and gifts to the poor have ascended as a memorial offering before God.
bsb.10:5: Now send men to Joppa to call for a man named Simon who is called Peter.
bsb.10:6: He is staying with Simon the tanner, whose house is by the sea.”
bsb.10:7: When the angel who spoke to him had gone, Cornelius called two of his servants and a devout soldier from among his attendants.
bsb.10:8: He explained what had happened and sent them to Joppa.
bsb.10:9: The next day at about the sixth hour, as the men were approaching the city on their journey, Peter went up on the roof to pray.
bsb.10:10: He became hungry and wanted something to eat, but while the meal was being prepared, he fell into a trance.
bsb.10:11: He saw heaven open and something like a large sheet being let down to earth by its four corners.
bsb.10:12: It contained all kinds of four-footed animals and reptiles of the earth, as well as birds of the air.
bsb.10:13: Then a voice said to him: “Get up, Peter, kill and eat!”
bsb.10:14: “No, Lord!” Peter answered. “I have never eaten anything impure or unclean.”
bsb.10:15: The voice spoke to him a second time: “Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.”
bsb.10:16: This happened three times, and all at once the sheet was taken back up into heaven.
bsb.10:17: While Peter was puzzling over the meaning of the vision, the men sent by Cornelius found Simon’s house and approached the gate.
bsb.10:18: They called out to ask if Simon called Peter was staying there.
bsb.10:19: As Peter continued to reflect on the vision, the Spirit said to him, “Behold, three men are looking for you.
bsb.10:20: So get up! Go downstairs and accompany them without hesitation, because I have sent them.”
bsb.10:21: So Peter went down to the men and said, “Here am I, the one you are looking for. Why have you come?”
bsb.10:22: “Cornelius the centurion has sent us,” they said. “He is a righteous and God-fearing man with a good reputation among the whole Jewish nation. A holy angel instructed him to request your presence in his home so he could hear a message from you.”
bsb.10:23: So Peter invited them in as his guests. And the next day he got ready and went with them, accompanied by some of the brothers from Joppa.
bsb.10:24: The following day he arrived in Caesarea, where Cornelius was expecting them and had called together his relatives and close friends.
bsb.10:25: As Peter was about to enter, Cornelius met him and fell at his feet to worship him.
bsb.10:26: But Peter helped him up. “Stand up,” he said, “I am only a man myself.”
bsb.10:27: As Peter talked with him, he went inside and found many people gathered together.
bsb.10:28: He said to them, “You know how unlawful it is for a Jew to associate with a foreigner or visit him. But God has shown me that I should not call any man impure or unclean.
bsb.10:29: So when I was invited, I came without objection. I ask, then, why have you sent for me?”
bsb.10:30: Cornelius answered: “Four days ago I was in my house praying at this, the ninth hour. Suddenly a man in radiant clothing stood before me
bsb.10:31: and said, ‘Cornelius, your prayer has been heard, and your gifts to the poor have been remembered before God.
bsb.10:32: Therefore send to Joppa for Simon, who is called Peter. He is a guest in the home of Simon the tanner, by the sea.’
bsb.10:33: So I sent for you immediately, and you were kind enough to come. Now then, we are all here in the presence of God to listen to everything the Lord has instructed you to tell us.”
bsb.10:34: Then Peter began to speak: “I now truly understand that God does not show favoritism,
bsb.10:35: but welcomes those from every nation who fear Him and do what is right.
bsb.10:36: He has sent this message to the people of Israel, proclaiming the gospel of peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all.
bsb.10:37: You yourselves know what has happened throughout Judea, beginning in Galilee with the baptism that John proclaimed:
bsb.10:38: how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power, and how Jesus went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, because God was with Him.
bsb.10:39: We are witnesses of all that He did, both in the land of the Jews and in Jerusalem. And although they put Him to death by hanging Him on a tree,
bsb.10:40: God raised Him up on the third day and caused Him to be seen—
bsb.10:41: not by all the people, but by the witnesses God had chosen beforehand, by us who ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead.
bsb.10:42: And He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that He is the One appointed by God to judge the living and the dead.
bsb.10:43: All the prophets testify about Him that everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name.”
bsb.10:44: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all who heard his message.
bsb.10:45: All the circumcised believers who had accompanied Peter were astounded that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles.
bsb.10:46: For they heard them speaking in tongues and exalting God. Then Peter said,
bsb.10:47: “Can anyone withhold the water to baptize these people? They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have!”
bsb.10:48: So he ordered that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to stay for a few days.
bsb.11:1: The apostles and brothers throughout Judea soon heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God.
bsb.11:2: So when Peter went up to Jerusalem, the circumcised believers took issue with him
bsb.11:3: and said, “You visited uncircumcised men and ate with them.”
bsb.11:4: But Peter began and explained to them the whole sequence of events:
bsb.11:5: “I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision of something like a large sheet being let down from heaven by its four corners, and it came right down to me.
bsb.11:6: I looked at it closely and saw four-footed animals of the earth, wild beasts, reptiles, and birds of the air.
bsb.11:7: Then I heard a voice saying to me, ‘Get up, Peter, kill and eat.’
bsb.11:8: ‘No, Lord,’ I said, ‘for nothing impure or unclean has ever entered my mouth.’
bsb.11:9: But the voice spoke from heaven a second time, ‘Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.’
bsb.11:10: This happened three times, and everything was drawn back up into heaven.
bsb.11:11: Just then three men sent to me from Caesarea stopped at the house where I was staying.
bsb.11:12: The Spirit told me to accompany them without hesitation. These six brothers also went with me, and we entered the man’s home.
bsb.11:13: He told us how he had seen an angel standing in his house and saying, ‘Send to Joppa for Simon who is called Peter.
bsb.11:14: He will convey to you a message by which you and all your household will be saved.’
bsb.11:15: As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them, just as He had fallen upon us at the beginning.
bsb.11:16: Then I remembered the word of the Lord, as He used to say, ‘John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’
bsb.11:17: So if God gave them the same gift He gave us who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to hinder the work of God?”
bsb.11:18: When they heard this, their objections were put to rest, and they glorified God, saying, “So then, God has granted even the Gentiles repentance unto life.”
bsb.11:19: Meanwhile those scattered by the persecution that began with Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the message only to Jews.
bsb.11:20: But some of them, men from Cyprus and Cyrene, went to Antioch and began speaking to the Greeks as well, proclaiming the good news about the Lord Jesus.
bsb.11:21: The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number of people believed and turned to the Lord.
bsb.11:22: When news of this reached the ears of the church in Jerusalem, they sent Barnabas to Antioch.
bsb.11:23: When he arrived and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced and encouraged them all to abide in the Lord with all their hearts.
bsb.11:24: Barnabas was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith, and a great number of people were brought to the Lord.
bsb.11:25: Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul,
bsb.11:26: and when he found him, he brought him back to Antioch. So for a full year they met together with the church and taught large numbers of people. The disciples were first called Christians at Antioch.
bsb.11:27: In those days some prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
bsb.11:28: One of them named Agabus stood up and predicted through the Spirit that a great famine would sweep across the whole world. (This happened under Claudius.)
bsb.11:29: So the disciples, each according to his ability, decided to send relief to the brothers living in Judea.
bsb.11:30: This they did, sending their gifts to the elders with Barnabas and Saul.
bsb.12:1: About that time, King Herod reached out to harm some who belonged to the church.
bsb.12:2: He had James, the brother of John, put to death with the sword.
bsb.12:3: And seeing that this pleased the Jews, Herod proceeded to seize Peter during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
bsb.12:4: He arrested him and put him in prison, handing him over to be guarded by four squads of four soldiers each. Herod intended to bring him out to the people after the Passover.
bsb.12:5: So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was fervently praying to God for him.
bsb.12:6: On the night before Herod was to bring him to trial, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, with sentries standing guard at the entrance to the prison.
bsb.12:7: Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared and a light shone in the cell. He tapped Peter on the side and woke him up, saying, “Get up quickly.” And the chains fell off his wrists.
bsb.12:8: “Get dressed and put on your sandals,” said the angel. Peter did so, and the angel told him, “Wrap your cloak around you and follow me.”
bsb.12:9: So Peter followed him out, but he was unaware that what the angel was doing was real. He thought he was only seeing a vision.
bsb.12:10: They passed the first and second guards and came to the iron gate leading to the city, which opened for them by itself. When they had gone outside and walked the length of one block, the angel suddenly left him.
bsb.12:11: Then Peter came to himself and said, “Now I know for sure that the Lord has sent His angel and rescued me from Herod’s grasp and from everything the Jewish people were anticipating.”
bsb.12:12: And when he had realized this, he went to the house of Mary the mother of John, also called Mark, where many people had gathered together and were praying.
bsb.12:13: He knocked at the outer gate, and a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer it.
bsb.12:14: When she recognized Peter’s voice, she was so overjoyed that she forgot to open the gate, but ran inside and announced, “Peter is standing at the gate!”
bsb.12:15: “You are out of your mind,” they told her. But when she kept insisting it was so, they said, “It must be his angel.”
bsb.12:16: But Peter kept on knocking, and when they opened the door and saw him, they were astounded.
bsb.12:17: Peter motioned with his hand for silence, and he described how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. “Send word to James and to the brothers,” he said, and he left for another place.
bsb.12:18: At daybreak there was no small commotion among the soldiers as to what had become of Peter.
bsb.12:19: After Herod had searched for him unsuccessfully, he examined the guards and ordered that they be executed. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and spent some time there.
bsb.12:20: Now Herod was in a furious dispute with the people of Tyre and Sidon, and they convened before him. Having secured the support of Blastus, the king’s chamberlain, they asked for peace, because their region depended on the king’s country for food.
bsb.12:21: On the appointed day, Herod donned his royal robes, sat on his throne, and addressed the people.
bsb.12:22: And they began to shout, “This is the voice of a god, not a man!”
bsb.12:23: Immediately, because Herod did not give glory to God, an angel of the Lord struck him down, and he was eaten by worms and died.
bsb.12:24: But the word of God continued to spread and multiply.
bsb.12:25: When Barnabas and Saul had fulfilled their mission to Jerusalem, they returned, bringing with them John, also called Mark.
bsb.13:1: Now in the church at Antioch there were prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen (who had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch), and Saul.
bsb.13:2: While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, “Set apart for Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.”
bsb.13:3: And after they had fasted and prayed, they laid their hands on them and sent them off.
bsb.13:4: So Barnabas and Saul, sent forth by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia and sailed from there to Cyprus.
bsb.13:5: When they arrived at Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the Jewish synagogues. And John was with them as their helper.
bsb.13:6: They traveled through the whole island as far as Paphos, where they found a Jewish sorcerer and false prophet named Bar-Jesus,
bsb.13:7: an attendant of the proconsul, Sergius Paulus. The proconsul, a man of intelligence, summoned Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear the word of God.
bsb.13:8: But Elymas the sorcerer (for that is what his name means) opposed them and tried to turn the proconsul from the faith.
bsb.13:9: Then Saul, who was also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked directly at Elymas
bsb.13:10: and said, “O child of the devil and enemy of all righteousness, you are full of all kinds of deceit and trickery! Will you never stop perverting the straight ways of the Lord?
bsb.13:11: Now look, the hand of the Lord is against you, and for a time you will be blind and unable to see the light of the sun.” Immediately mist and darkness came over him, and he groped about, seeking someone to lead him by the hand.
bsb.13:12: When the proconsul saw what had happened, he believed, for he was astonished at the teaching about the Lord.
bsb.13:13: After setting sail from Paphos, Paul and his companions came to Perga in Pamphylia, where John left them to return to Jerusalem.
bsb.13:14: And from Perga, they traveled inland to Pisidian Antioch, where they entered the synagogue on the Sabbath and sat down.
bsb.13:15: After the reading from the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue leaders sent word to them: “Brothers, if you have a word of encouragement for the people, please speak.”
bsb.13:16: Paul stood up, motioned with his hand, and began to speak: “Men of Israel and you Gentiles who fear God, listen to me!
bsb.13:17: The God of the people of Israel chose our fathers. He made them into a great people during their stay in Egypt, and with an uplifted arm He led them out of that land.
bsb.13:18: He endured their conduct for about forty years in the wilderness.
bsb.13:19: And having vanquished seven nations in Canaan, He gave their land to His people as an inheritance.
bsb.13:20: All this took about 450 years. After this, God gave them judges until the time of Samuel the prophet.
bsb.13:21: Then the people asked for a king, and God gave them forty years under Saul son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin.
bsb.13:22: After removing Saul, He raised up David as their king and testified about him: ‘I have found David son of Jesse a man after My own heart; he will carry out My will in its entirety.’
bsb.13:23: From the descendants of this man, God has brought to Israel the Savior Jesus, as He promised.
bsb.13:24: Before the arrival of Jesus, John preached a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.
bsb.13:25: As John was completing his course, he said, ‘Who do you suppose I am? I am not that One. But He is coming after me whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.’
bsb.13:26: Brothers, children of Abraham, and you Gentiles who fear God, it is to us that this message of salvation has been sent.
bsb.13:27: The people of Jerusalem and their rulers did not recognize Jesus, yet in condemning Him they fulfilled the words of the prophets that are read every Sabbath.
bsb.13:28: And though they found no ground for a death sentence, they asked Pilate to have Him executed.
bsb.13:29: When they had carried out all that was written about Him, they took Him down from the tree and laid Him in a tomb.
bsb.13:30: But God raised Him from the dead,
bsb.13:31: and for many days He was seen by those who had accompanied Him from Galilee to Jerusalem. They are now His witnesses to our people.
bsb.13:32: And now we proclaim to you the good news: What God promised our fathers
bsb.13:33: He has fulfilled for us, their children, by raising up Jesus. As it is written in the second Psalm: ‘You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.’
bsb.13:34: In fact, God raised Him from the dead, never to see decay. As He has said: ‘I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.’
bsb.13:35: So also, He says in another Psalm: ‘You will not let Your Holy One see decay.’
bsb.13:36: For when David had served God’s purpose in his own generation, he fell asleep. His body was buried with his fathers and saw decay.
bsb.13:37: But the One whom God raised from the dead did not see decay.
bsb.13:38: Therefore let it be known to you, brothers, that through Jesus the forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you.
bsb.13:39: Through Him everyone who believes is justified from everything you could not be justified from by the law of Moses.
bsb.13:40: Watch out, then, that what was spoken by the prophets does not happen to you:
bsb.13:41: ‘Look, you scoffers, wonder and perish! For I am doing a work in your days that you would never believe, even if someone told you.’”
bsb.13:42: As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the people urged them to continue this message on the next Sabbath.
bsb.13:43: After the synagogue was dismissed, many of the Jews and devout converts to Judaism followed Paul and Barnabas, who spoke to them and urged them to continue in the grace of God.
bsb.13:44: On the following Sabbath, nearly the whole city gathered to hear the word of the Lord.
bsb.13:45: But when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy, and they blasphemously contradicted what Paul was saying.
bsb.13:46: Then Paul and Barnabas answered them boldly: “It was necessary to speak the word of God to you first. But since you reject it and do not consider yourselves worthy of eternal life, we now turn to the Gentiles.
bsb.13:47: For this is what the Lord has commanded us: ‘I have made you a light for the Gentiles, to bring salvation to the ends of the earth.’”
bsb.13:48: When the Gentiles heard this, they rejoiced and glorified the word of the Lord, and all who were appointed for eternal life believed.
bsb.13:49: And the word of the Lord spread throughout that region.
bsb.13:50: The Jews, however, incited the religious women of prominence and the leading men of the city. They stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas and drove them out of their district.
bsb.13:51: So they shook the dust off their feet in protest against them and went to Iconium.
bsb.13:52: And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
bsb.14:1: At Iconium, Paul and Barnabas went as usual into the Jewish synagogue, where they spoke so well that a great number of Jews and Greeks believed.
bsb.14:2: But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles and poisoned their minds against the brothers.
bsb.14:3: So Paul and Barnabas spent considerable time there, speaking boldly for the Lord, who affirmed the message of His grace by enabling them to perform signs and wonders.
bsb.14:4: The people of the city were divided. Some sided with the Jews, and others with the apostles.
bsb.14:5: But when the Gentiles and Jews, together with their rulers, set out to mistreat and stone them,
bsb.14:6: they found out about it and fled to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe and to the surrounding region,
bsb.14:7: where they continued to preach the gospel.
bsb.14:8: In Lystra there sat a man crippled in his feet, who was lame from birth and had never walked.
bsb.14:9: This man was listening to the words of Paul, who looked intently at him and saw that he had faith to be healed.
bsb.14:10: In a loud voice Paul called out, “Stand up on your feet!” And the man jumped up and began to walk.
bsb.14:11: When the crowds saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices in the Lycaonian language: “The gods have come down to us in human form!”
bsb.14:12: Barnabas they called Zeus, and Paul they called Hermes, because he was the chief speaker.
bsb.14:13: The priest of Zeus, whose temple was just outside the city, brought bulls and wreaths to the city gates, hoping to offer a sacrifice along with the crowds.
bsb.14:14: But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul found out about this, they tore their clothes and rushed into the crowd, shouting,
bsb.14:15: “Men, why are you doing this? We too are only men, human like you. We are bringing you good news that you should turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and sea and everything in them.
bsb.14:16: In past generations, He let all nations go their own way.
bsb.14:17: Yet He has not left Himself without testimony to His goodness: He gives you rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.”
bsb.14:18: Even with these words, Paul and Barnabas could hardly stop the crowds from sacrificing to them.
bsb.14:19: Then some Jews arrived from Antioch and Iconium and won over the crowds. They stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, presuming he was dead.
bsb.14:20: But after the disciples had gathered around him, he got up and went back into the city. And the next day he left with Barnabas for Derbe.
bsb.14:21: They preached the gospel to that city and made many disciples. Then they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,
bsb.14:22: strengthening the souls of the disciples and encouraging them to continue in the faith. “We must endure many hardships to enter the kingdom of God,” they said.
bsb.14:23: Paul and Barnabas appointed elders for them in each church, praying and fasting as they entrusted them to the Lord, in whom they had believed.
bsb.14:24: After passing through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.
bsb.14:25: And when they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.
bsb.14:26: From Attalia they sailed to Antioch, where they had been commended to the grace of God for the work they had just completed.
bsb.14:27: When they arrived, they gathered the church together and reported all that God had done through them, and how He had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.
bsb.14:28: And they spent a long time there with the disciples.
bsb.15:1: Then some men came down from Judea and were teaching the brothers, “Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved.”
bsb.15:2: And after engaging these men in sharp debate, Paul and Barnabas were appointed, along with some other believers, to go up to Jerusalem to see the apostles and elders about this question.
bsb.15:3: Sent on their way by the church, they passed through Phoenicia and Samaria, recounting the conversion of the Gentiles and bringing great joy to all the brothers.
bsb.15:4: On their arrival in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church and apostles and elders, to whom they reported all that God had done through them.
bsb.15:5: But some believers from the party of the Pharisees stood up and declared, “The Gentiles must be circumcised and required to obey the law of Moses.”
bsb.15:6: So the apostles and elders met to look into this matter.
bsb.15:7: After much discussion, Peter got up and said to them, “Brothers, you know that in the early days God made a choice among you that the Gentiles would hear from my lips the message of the gospel and believe.
bsb.15:8: And God, who knows the heart, showed His approval by giving the Holy Spirit to them, just as He did to us.
bsb.15:9: He made no distinction between us and them, for He cleansed their hearts by faith.
bsb.15:10: Now then, why do you test God by placing on the necks of the disciples a yoke that neither we nor our fathers have been able to bear?
bsb.15:11: On the contrary, we believe it is through the grace of the Lord Jesus that we are saved, just as they are.”
bsb.15:12: The whole assembly fell silent as they listened to Barnabas and Paul describing the signs and wonders God had done among the Gentiles through them.
bsb.15:13: When they had finished speaking, James declared, “Brothers, listen to me!
bsb.15:14: Simon has told us how God first visited the Gentiles to take from them a people to be His own.
bsb.15:15: The words of the prophets agree with this, as it is written:
bsb.15:16: ‘After this I will return and rebuild the fallen tent of David. Its ruins I will rebuild, and I will restore it,
bsb.15:17: so that the remnant of men may seek the Lord, and all the Gentiles who are called by My name, says the Lord who does these things
bsb.15:18: that have been known for ages.’
bsb.15:19: It is my judgment, therefore, that we should not cause trouble for the Gentiles who are turning to God.
bsb.15:20: Instead, we should write and tell them to abstain from food polluted by idols, from sexual immorality, from the meat of strangled animals, and from blood.
bsb.15:21: For Moses has been proclaimed in every city from ancient times and is read in the synagogues on every Sabbath.”
bsb.15:22: Then the apostles and elders, with the whole church, decided to select men from among them to send to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas called Barsabbas and Silas, two leaders among the brothers,
bsb.15:23: and sent them with this letter: The apostles and the elders, your brothers, To the brothers among the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: Greetings.
bsb.15:24: It has come to our attention that some went out from us without our authorization and unsettled you, troubling your minds by what they said.
bsb.15:25: So we all agreed to choose men to send to you along with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
bsb.15:26: men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
bsb.15:27: Therefore we are sending Judas and Silas to tell you in person the same things we are writing.
bsb.15:28: It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us not to burden you with anything beyond these essential requirements:
bsb.15:29: You must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality. You will do well to avoid these things. Farewell.
bsb.15:30: So the men were sent off and went down to Antioch, where they assembled the congregation and delivered the letter.
bsb.15:31: When the people read it, they rejoiced at its encouraging message.
bsb.15:32: Judas and Silas, who themselves were prophets, said much to encourage and strengthen the brothers.
bsb.15:33: After spending some time there, they were sent off by the brothers in peace to return to those who had sent them.
bsb.15:35: But Paul and Barnabas remained at Antioch, along with many others, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord.
bsb.15:36: Some time later Paul said to Barnabas, “Let us go back and visit the brothers in every town where we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing.”
bsb.15:37: Barnabas wanted to take John, also called Mark.
bsb.15:38: But Paul thought it best not to take him, because he had deserted them in Pamphylia and had not accompanied them in the work.
bsb.15:39: Their disagreement was so sharp that they parted company. Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus,
bsb.15:40: but Paul chose Silas and left, commended by the brothers to the grace of the Lord.
bsb.15:41: And he traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
bsb.16:1: Paul came to Derbe and then to Lystra, where he found a disciple named Timothy, the son of a believing Jewish woman and a Greek father.
bsb.16:2: The brothers in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of him.
bsb.16:3: Paul wanted Timothy to accompany him, so he took him and circumcised him on account of the Jews in that area, for they all knew that his father was a Greek.
bsb.16:4: As they went from town to town, they delivered the decisions handed down by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem for the people to obey.
bsb.16:5: So the churches were strengthened in the faith and grew daily in numbers.
bsb.16:6: After the Holy Spirit had prevented them from speaking the word in the province of Asia, they traveled through the region of Phrygia and Galatia.
bsb.16:7: And when they came to the border of Mysia, they tried to enter Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not permit them.
bsb.16:8: So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.
bsb.16:9: During the night, Paul had a vision of a man of Macedonia standing and pleading with him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us.”
bsb.16:10: As soon as Paul had seen the vision, we got ready to leave for Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them.
bsb.16:11: We sailed from Troas straight to Samothrace, and the following day on to Neapolis.
bsb.16:12: From there we went to the Roman colony of Philippi, the leading city of that district of Macedonia. And we stayed there several days.
bsb.16:13: On the Sabbath we went outside the city gate along the river, where it was customary to find a place of prayer. After sitting down, we spoke to the women who had gathered there.
bsb.16:14: Among those listening was a woman named Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, who was a worshiper of God. The Lord opened her heart to respond to Paul’s message.
bsb.16:15: And when she and her household had been baptized, she urged us, “If you consider me a believer in the Lord, come and stay at my house.” And she persuaded us.
bsb.16:16: One day as we were going to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl with a spirit of divination, who earned a large income for her masters by fortune-telling.
bsb.16:17: This girl followed Paul and the rest of us, shouting, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who are proclaiming to you the way of salvation!”
bsb.16:18: She continued this for many days. Eventually Paul grew so aggravated that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her!” And the spirit left her at that very moment.
bsb.16:19: When the girl’s owners saw that their hope of making money was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them before the authorities in the marketplace.
bsb.16:20: They brought them to the magistrates and said, “These men are Jews and are throwing our city into turmoil
bsb.16:21: by promoting customs that are unlawful for us Romans to adopt or practice.”
bsb.16:22: The crowd joined in the attack against Paul and Silas, and the magistrates ordered that they be stripped and beaten with rods.
bsb.16:23: And after striking them with many blows, they threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to guard them securely.
bsb.16:24: On receiving this order, he placed them in the inner cell and fastened their feet in the stocks.
bsb.16:25: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.
bsb.16:26: Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the foundations of the prison. At once all the doors flew open and everyone’s chains came loose.
bsb.16:27: When the jailer woke up and saw the prison doors open, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself, presuming that the prisoners had escaped.
bsb.16:28: But Paul called out in a loud voice, “Do not harm yourself! We are all here!”
bsb.16:29: Calling for lights, the jailer rushed in and fell trembling before Paul and Silas.
bsb.16:30: Then he brought them out and asked, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”
bsb.16:31: They replied, “Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved, you and your household.”
bsb.16:32: Then Paul and Silas spoke the word of the Lord to him and to everyone in his house.
bsb.16:33: At that hour of the night, the jailer took them and washed their wounds. And without delay, he and all his household were baptized.
bsb.16:34: Then he brought them into his home and set a meal before them. So he and all his household rejoiced that they had come to believe in God.
bsb.16:35: When daylight came, the magistrates sent their officers with the order: “Release those men.”
bsb.16:36: The jailer informed Paul: “The magistrates have sent orders to release you. Now you may go on your way in peace.”
bsb.16:37: But Paul said to the officers, “They beat us publicly without a trial and threw us into prison, even though we are Roman citizens. And now do they want to send us away secretly? Absolutely not! Let them come themselves and escort us out!”
bsb.16:38: So the officers relayed this message to the magistrates, who were alarmed to hear that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens.
bsb.16:39: They came to appease them and led them out, requesting that they leave the city.
bsb.16:40: After Paul and Silas came out of the prison, they went to Lydia’s house to see the brothers and encourage them. Then they left the city.
bsb.17:1: When they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.
bsb.17:2: As was his custom, Paul went into the synagogue, and on three Sabbaths he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,
bsb.17:3: explaining and proving that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead. “This Jesus I am proclaiming to you is the Christ,” he declared.
bsb.17:4: Some of the Jews were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, along with a large number of God-fearing Greeks and quite a few leading women.
bsb.17:5: The Jews, however, became jealous. So they brought in some troublemakers from the marketplace, formed a mob, and sent the city into an uproar. They raided Jason’s house in search of Paul and Silas, hoping to bring them out to the people.
bsb.17:6: But when they could not find them, they dragged Jason and some other brothers before the city officials, shouting, “These men who have turned the world upside down have now come here,
bsb.17:7: and Jason has welcomed them into his home. They are all defying Caesar’s decrees, saying that there is another king, named Jesus!”
bsb.17:8: On hearing this, the crowd and city officials were greatly disturbed.
bsb.17:9: And they collected bond from Jason and the others, and then released them.
bsb.17:10: As soon as night had fallen, the brothers sent Paul and Silas away to Berea. On arriving there, they went into the Jewish synagogue.
bsb.17:11: Now the Bereans were more noble-minded than the Thessalonians, for they received the message with great eagerness and examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true.
bsb.17:12: As a result, many of them believed, along with quite a few prominent Greek women and men.
bsb.17:13: But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that Paul was also proclaiming the word of God in Berea, they went there themselves to incite and agitate the crowds.
bsb.17:14: The brothers immediately sent Paul to the coast, but Silas and Timothy remained in Berea.
bsb.17:15: Those who escorted Paul brought him to Athens and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible.
bsb.17:16: While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, he was deeply disturbed in his spirit to see that the city was full of idols.
bsb.17:17: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and God-fearing Gentiles, and in the marketplace with those he met each day.
bsb.17:18: Some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also began to debate with him. Some of them asked, “What is this babbler trying to say?” Others said, “He seems to be advocating foreign gods.” They said this because Paul was proclaiming the good news of Jesus and the resurrection.
bsb.17:19: So they took Paul and brought him to the Areopagus, where they asked him, “May we know what this new teaching is that you are presenting?
bsb.17:20: For you are bringing some strange notions to our ears, and we want to know what they mean.”
bsb.17:21: Now all the Athenians and foreigners who lived there spent their time doing nothing more than hearing and articulating new ideas.
bsb.17:22: Then Paul stood up in the meeting of the Areopagus and said, “Men of Athens, I see that in every way you are very religious.
bsb.17:23: For as I walked around and examined your objects of worship, I even found an altar with this inscription: TO AN UNKNOWN GOD. Therefore what you worship as something unknown, I now proclaim to you.
bsb.17:24: The God who made the world and everything in it is the Lord of heaven and earth and does not live in temples made by human hands.
bsb.17:25: Nor is He served by human hands, as if He needed anything, because He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything else.
bsb.17:26: From one man He made every nation of men, that they should inhabit the whole earth; and He determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their lands.
bsb.17:27: God intended that they would seek Him and perhaps reach out for Him and find Him, though He is not far from each one of us.
bsb.17:28: ‘For in Him we live and move and have our being.’ As some of your own poets have said, ‘We are His offspring.’
bsb.17:29: Therefore, being offspring of God, we should not think that the Divine Being is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by man’s skill and imagination.
bsb.17:30: Although God overlooked the ignorance of earlier times, He now commands all people everywhere to repent.
bsb.17:31: For He has set a day when He will judge the world with justice by the Man He has appointed. He has given proof of this to everyone by raising Him from the dead.”
bsb.17:32: When they heard about the resurrection of the dead, some began to mock him, but others said, “We want to hear you again on this topic.”
bsb.17:33: At that, Paul left the Areopagus.
bsb.17:34: But some joined him and believed, including Dionysius the Areopagite, a woman named Damaris, and others who were with them.
bsb.18:1: After this, Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.
bsb.18:2: There he found a Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome. Paul went to visit them,
bsb.18:3: and he stayed and worked with them because they were tentmakers by trade, just as he was.
bsb.18:4: Every Sabbath he reasoned in the synagogue, trying to persuade Jews and Greeks alike.
bsb.18:5: And when Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul devoted himself fully to the word, testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.
bsb.18:6: But when they opposed and insulted him, he shook out his garments and told them, “Your blood be on your own heads! I am innocent of it. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.”
bsb.18:7: So Paul left the synagogue and went next door to the house of Titus Justus, a worshiper of God.
bsb.18:8: Crispus, the synagogue leader, and his whole household believed in the Lord. And many of the Corinthians who heard the message believed and were baptized.
bsb.18:9: One night the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision: “Do not be afraid; keep on speaking; do not be silent.
bsb.18:10: For I am with you and no one will lay a hand on you, because I have many people in this city.”
bsb.18:11: So Paul stayed for a year and a half, teaching the word of God among the Corinthians.
bsb.18:12: While Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews coordinated an attack on Paul and brought him before the judgment seat.
bsb.18:13: “This man is persuading the people to worship God in ways contrary to the law,” they said.
bsb.18:14: But just as Paul was about to speak, Gallio told the Jews, “If this matter involved a wrongdoing or vicious crime, O Jews, it would be reasonable for me to hear your complaint.
bsb.18:15: But since it is a dispute about words and names and your own law, settle it yourselves. I refuse to be a judge of such things.”
bsb.18:16: And he drove them away from the judgment seat.
bsb.18:17: At this, the crowd seized Sosthenes the synagogue leader and beat him in front of the judgment seat. But none of this was of concern to Gallio.
bsb.18:18: Paul remained in Corinth for quite some time before saying goodbye to the brothers. He had his head shaved in Cenchrea to keep a vow he had made, and then he sailed for Syria, accompanied by Priscilla and Aquila.
bsb.18:19: When they reached Ephesus, Paul parted ways with Priscilla and Aquila. He himself went into the synagogue there and reasoned with the Jews.
bsb.18:20: When they asked him to stay for a while longer, he declined.
bsb.18:21: But as he left, he said, “I will come back to you if God is willing.” And he set sail from Ephesus.
bsb.18:22: When Paul had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the church at Jerusalem. Then he went down to Antioch.
bsb.18:23: After Paul had spent some time in Antioch, he traveled from place to place throughout the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.
bsb.18:24: Meanwhile a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent man, well versed in the Scriptures.
bsb.18:25: He had been instructed in the way of the Lord and was fervent in spirit. He spoke and taught accurately about Jesus, though he knew only the baptism of John.
bsb.18:26: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him in and explained to him the way of God more accurately.
bsb.18:27: When Apollos resolved to cross over to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples there to welcome him. On his arrival, he was a great help to those who by grace had believed.
bsb.18:28: For he powerfully refuted the Jews in public debate, proving from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.
bsb.19:1: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul passed through the interior and came to Ephesus. There he found some disciples
bsb.19:2: and asked them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you became believers?” “No,” they answered, “we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”
bsb.19:3: “Into what, then, were you baptized?” Paul asked. “The baptism of John,” they replied.
bsb.19:4: Paul explained: “John’s baptism was a baptism of repentance. He told the people to believe in the One coming after him, that is, in Jesus.”
bsb.19:5: On hearing this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
bsb.19:6: And when Paul laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied.
bsb.19:7: There were about twelve men in all.
bsb.19:8: Then Paul went into the synagogue and spoke boldly there for three months, arguing persuasively about the kingdom of God.
bsb.19:9: But when some of them stubbornly refused to believe and publicly maligned the Way, Paul took his disciples and left the synagogue to conduct daily discussions in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.
bsb.19:10: This continued for two years, so that everyone who lived in the province of Asia, Jews and Greeks alike, heard the word of the Lord.
bsb.19:11: God did extraordinary miracles through the hands of Paul,
bsb.19:12: so that even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched him were taken to the sick, and the diseases and evil spirits left them.
bsb.19:13: Now there were some itinerant Jewish exorcists who tried to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those with evil spirits. They would say, “I bind you by Jesus, whom Paul proclaims.”
bsb.19:14: Seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.
bsb.19:15: Eventually, one of the evil spirits answered them, “Jesus I know, and I know about Paul, but who are you?”
bsb.19:16: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and overpowered them all. The attack was so violent that they ran out of the house naked and wounded.
bsb.19:17: This became known to all the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus, and fear came over all of them. So the name of the Lord Jesus was held in high honor.
bsb.19:18: Many who had believed now came forward, confessing and disclosing their deeds.
bsb.19:19: And a number of those who had practiced magic arts brought their books and burned them in front of everyone. When the value of the books was calculated, the total came to fifty thousand drachmas.
bsb.19:20: So the word of the Lord powerfully continued to spread and prevail.
bsb.19:21: After these things had happened, Paul resolved in the Spirit to go to Jerusalem after he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia. “After I have been there,” he said, “I must see Rome as well.”
bsb.19:22: He sent two of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia, while he stayed for a time in the province of Asia.
bsb.19:23: About that time there arose a great disturbance about the Way.
bsb.19:24: It began with a silversmith named Demetrius who made silver shrines of Artemis, bringing much business to the craftsmen.
bsb.19:25: Demetrius assembled the craftsmen, along with the workmen in related trades. “Men,” he said, “you know that this business is our source of prosperity.
bsb.19:26: And you can see and hear that not only in Ephesus, but in nearly the whole province of Asia, Paul has persuaded a great number of people to turn away. He says that man-made gods are no gods at all.
bsb.19:27: There is danger not only that our business will fall into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be discredited and her majesty deposed—she who is worshiped by all the province of Asia and the whole world.”
bsb.19:28: When the men heard this, they were enraged and began shouting, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
bsb.19:29: Soon the whole city was in disarray. They rushed together into the theatre, dragging with them Gaius and Aristarchus, Paul’s traveling companions from Macedonia.
bsb.19:30: Paul wanted to go before the assembly, but the disciples would not allow him.
bsb.19:31: Even some of Paul’s friends who were officials of the province of Asia sent word to him, begging him not to venture into the theatre.
bsb.19:32: Meanwhile the assembly was in turmoil. Some were shouting one thing and some another, and most of them did not even know why they were there.
bsb.19:33: The Jews in the crowd pushed Alexander forward to explain himself, and he motioned for silence so he could make his defense to the people.
bsb.19:34: But when they realized that he was a Jew, they all shouted in unison for about two hours: “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
bsb.19:35: Finally the city clerk quieted the crowd and declared, “Men of Ephesus, doesn’t everyone know that the city of Ephesus is guardian of the temple of the great Artemis and of her image, which fell from heaven?
bsb.19:36: Since these things are undeniable, you ought to be calm and not do anything rash.
bsb.19:37: For you have brought these men here, though they have neither robbed our temple nor blasphemed our goddess.
bsb.19:38: So if Demetrius and his fellow craftsmen have a complaint against anyone, the courts are open and proconsuls are available. Let them bring charges against one another there.
bsb.19:39: But if you are seeking anything beyond this, it must be settled in a legal assembly.
bsb.19:40: For we are in jeopardy of being charged with rioting for today’s events, and we have no justification to account for this commotion.”
bsb.19:41: After he had said this, he dismissed the assembly.
bsb.20:1: When the uproar had ended, Paul sent for the disciples. And after encouraging them, he said goodbye to them and left for Macedonia.
bsb.20:2: After traveling through that area and speaking many words of encouragement, he arrived in Greece,
bsb.20:3: where he stayed three months. And when the Jews formed a plot against him as he was about to sail for Syria, he decided to go back through Macedonia.
bsb.20:4: Paul was accompanied by Sopater son of Pyrrhus from Berea, Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica, Gaius from Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus from the province of Asia.
bsb.20:5: These men went on ahead and waited for us in Troas.
bsb.20:6: And after the Feast of Unleavened Bread, we sailed from Philippi, and five days later we rejoined them in Troas, where we stayed seven days.
bsb.20:7: On the first day of the week we came together to break bread. Since Paul was ready to leave the next day, he talked to them and kept on speaking until midnight.
bsb.20:8: Now there were many lamps in the upper room where we were gathered.
bsb.20:9: And a certain young man named Eutychus, seated in the window, was sinking into a deep sleep as Paul talked on and on. When he was sound asleep, he fell from the third story and was picked up dead.
bsb.20:10: But Paul went down, threw himself on the young man, and embraced him. “Do not be alarmed!” he said. “He is still alive!”
bsb.20:11: Then Paul went back upstairs, broke bread, and ate. And after speaking until daybreak, he departed.
bsb.20:12: And the people were greatly relieved to take the boy home alive.
bsb.20:13: We went on ahead to the ship and sailed to Assos, where we were to take Paul aboard. He had arranged this because he was going there on foot.
bsb.20:14: And when he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and went on to Mitylene.
bsb.20:15: Sailing on from there, we arrived the next day opposite Chios. The day after that we arrived at Samos, and on the following day we came to Miletus.
bsb.20:16: Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus to avoid spending time in the province of Asia, because he was in a hurry to reach Jerusalem, if possible, by the day of Pentecost.
bsb.20:17: From Miletus, Paul sent to Ephesus for the elders of the church.
bsb.20:18: When they came to him, he said, “You know how I lived the whole time I was with you, from the first day I arrived in the province of Asia.
bsb.20:19: I served the Lord with great humility and with tears, especially in the trials that came upon me through the plots of the Jews.
bsb.20:20: I did not shrink back from declaring anything that was helpful to you as I taught you publicly and from house to house,
bsb.20:21: testifying to Jews and Greeks alike about repentance to God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ.
bsb.20:22: And now, compelled by the Spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there.
bsb.20:23: I only know that in town after town the Holy Spirit warns me that chains and afflictions await me.
bsb.20:24: But I consider my life of no value to me, if only I may finish my course and complete the ministry I have received from the Lord Jesus—the ministry of testifying to the good news of God’s grace.
bsb.20:25: Now I know that none of you among whom I have preached the kingdom will see my face again.
bsb.20:26: Therefore I testify to you this day that I am innocent of the blood of all men.
bsb.20:27: For I did not shrink back from declaring to you the whole will of God.
bsb.20:28: Keep watch over yourselves and the entire flock of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers. Be shepherds of the church of God, which He purchased with His own blood.
bsb.20:29: I know that after my departure, savage wolves will come in among you and will not spare the flock.
bsb.20:30: Even from your own number, men will rise up and distort the truth to draw away disciples after them.
bsb.20:31: Therefore be alert and remember that for three years I never stopped warning each of you night and day with tears.
bsb.20:32: And now I commit you to God and to the word of His grace, which can build you up and give you an inheritance among all who are sanctified.
bsb.20:33: I have not coveted anyone’s silver or gold or clothing.
bsb.20:34: You yourselves know that these hands of mine have ministered to my own needs and those of my companions.
bsb.20:35: In everything, I showed you that by this kind of hard work we must help the weak, remembering the words of the Lord Jesus Himself: ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”
bsb.20:36: When Paul had said this, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
bsb.20:37: They all wept openly as they embraced Paul and kissed him.
bsb.20:38: They were especially grieved by his statement that they would never see his face again. Then they accompanied him to the ship.
bsb.21:1: After we had torn ourselves away from them, we sailed directly to Cos, and the next day on to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
bsb.21:2: Finding a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we boarded it and set sail.
bsb.21:3: After sighting Cyprus and passing south of it, we sailed on to Syria and landed at Tyre, where the ship was to unload its cargo.
bsb.21:4: We sought out the disciples in Tyre and stayed with them seven days. Through the Spirit they kept telling Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.
bsb.21:5: But when our time there had ended, we set out on our journey. All the disciples, with their wives and children, accompanied us out of the city and knelt down on the beach to pray with us.
bsb.21:6: And after we had said our farewells, we went aboard the ship, and they returned home.
bsb.21:7: When we had finished our voyage from Tyre, we landed at Ptolemais, where we greeted the brothers and stayed with them for a day.
bsb.21:8: Leaving the next day, we went on to Caesarea and stayed at the home of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the Seven.
bsb.21:9: He had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.
bsb.21:10: After we had been there several days, a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.
bsb.21:11: Coming over to us, he took Paul’s belt, bound his own feet and hands, and said, “The Holy Spirit says: ‘In this way the Jews of Jerusalem will bind the owner of this belt and hand him over to the Gentiles.’”
bsb.21:12: When we heard this, we and the people there pleaded with Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.
bsb.21:13: Then Paul answered, “Why are you weeping and breaking my heart? I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”
bsb.21:14: When he would not be dissuaded, we fell silent and said, “The Lord’s will be done.”
bsb.21:15: After these days, we packed up and went on to Jerusalem.
bsb.21:16: Some of the disciples from Caesarea accompanied us, and they took us to stay at the home of Mnason the Cypriot, an early disciple.
bsb.21:17: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the brothers welcomed us joyfully.
bsb.21:18: The next day Paul went in with us to see James, and all the elders were present.
bsb.21:19: Paul greeted them and recounted one by one the things that God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.
bsb.21:20: When they heard this, they glorified God. Then they said to Paul, “You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews have believed, and all of them are zealous for the law.
bsb.21:21: But they are under the impression that you teach all the Jews who live among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children or observe our customs.
bsb.21:22: What then should we do? They will certainly hear that you have come.
bsb.21:23: Therefore do what we advise you. There are four men with us who have taken a vow.
